5. Corvinus hoc per congeriem be-
neficiorum effici, & Remonstrantes, vi sin-
gulari & admirabili fieri docent. At hic nihil
de infusione supernaturalis potentiæ, nihil de
gratia interna: totares per beneficia, morali
suasione moventia transfigitur. At vero tum
quando populum ex Ægypto deduxit, quo be-
neficio quid præstantius? Quando ad ipsos
liberandos, spoliis hostium ditandos, naturam
toties miraculis permultis commutavit,
mare rubrum divisit, luce & igne cælitus lucente
deduxit, hostes submerfit, ipsis novum
cor dederat, & legem cordi inscripferat,
quod aperte negat Deus. Ier. 31. v. 31. 32.
An non sic Moabitis, Ammonitis & Chaldæis novum
cor dedit?

page.notes: The numbered sections 4, 5 and 6 run into the lines in the printed text; I set each as its own paragraph. Some words are doubtful: "confolantem", "ambuletis", "infinuunt" and "totares" are copied as printed, not checked against a source. The "5." of the section numbers is an old-style figure; I wrote it as printed. Show-through and the edge marks on the margins are left out.
